cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's just been talking about Moses, Israel's leader, who put a veil over his face (2 Corinthians 3:13). Now Paul says God in His mercy has given him and the people with him this ministry.

cards.question: Since God gave them this ministry in His mercy, what does Paul say they don't do?

cards.text: Instead, Paul says they've renounced secret and shameful ways. Nothing tucked away in the back of a drawer, and trust me, friend, I know EXACTLY what ends up in the back of a drawer. ME.

cards.question: Paul says they don't practice deceit. True or false: he says they bend the word of God a little to win people over.
Paul says they commend themselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God by ___ proclamation of the truth.

cards.text: There's that veil again. Paul says if their gospel is veiled, it's veiled to those who are perishing.
Then Paul names who's behind it. The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers.

cards.question: Paul says the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers. What can't they see?
Paul says unbelievers can't see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ. True or false: he calls Christ the image of God.

cards.text: Then Paul makes it clear he doesn't proclaim himself. Paul's the delivery guy, friend, and NOBODY stares at the delivery guy when there's a box on the porch.

cards.question: Paul doesn't proclaim himself. So who does he proclaim?
Paul says he and the people with him are the Corinthians' ___ for Jesus' sake.

cards.text: Paul says God, who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness,' made His light shine in their hearts. Light in the dark? Friend, after YEARS in a junk drawer, that one hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Paul says God made His light shine in their hearts. True or false: he says that light gives them the knowledge of the glory of God in Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Now Paul paints a picture. They have this treasure in jars of clay, which is like keeping your whole paycheck in an old cookie box held shut with a rubber band.

cards.question: Why does Paul say they have this treasure in jars of clay?

answers.text: To show the power is from God

cards.text: So what's life like for a jar of clay? Paul lists the hits they take, and he answers every single one with 'but not.'

cards.question: Paul says they're hard pressed on all sides, but not ___.

cards.text: Next, perplexed, but not in despair, and persecuted, but not forsaken. Trouble keeps swinging, and Paul keeps popping back up like one of those inflatable punching bags: 'BUT NOT!'

cards.question: One more on Paul's list. He says they're struck down, but not what?

cards.text: Then Paul goes deeper. He says they always carry around in their body the death of Jesus.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says they carry the death of Jesus around so the life of Jesus may be revealed in their body.

cards.text: He says it another way: they're always consigned to death for Jesus' sake, so the life of Jesus may be revealed in their mortal body.

cards.question: So Paul sums it up: death is at work in them, but ___ is at work in the Corinthians.

cards.text: Then Paul points to what is written, where a psalmist says, 'I believed, therefore I have spoken' (Psalm 116:10). Paul says they have that same spirit of faith.

cards.question: With that same spirit of faith, Paul says they also believe and therefore ___.
True or false: Paul knows the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise them with Jesus.
Paul says God will raise them with Jesus. Who does Paul say God will present them together with, in His presence?

cards.text: Paul tells the Corinthians all this is for their benefit. God's grace keeps extending to more and more people.

cards.question: As grace reaches more and more people, what does Paul say it causes to overflow, to the glory of God?

cards.text: That line again: 'Therefore we do not lose heart.' Paul admits their outer self is wasting away, and I feel that, friend, because my edges once got so soft my cookies came out looking like weather maps.

cards.question: Paul says their outer self is wasting away. True or false: he says their inner self is being renewed day by day.

cards.text: Then Paul calls their troubles 'light and momentary affliction.' This man got STRUCK DOWN and calls it light, and I bumped my base on an oven door once and lay down for the whole afternoon.

cards.question: What does Paul say this light and momentary affliction is producing for them?

answers.text: A good name in every church

cards.text: So Paul tells them where they fix their eyes: not on what is seen, but on what is unseen.

cards.question: Why do Paul and the people with him fix their eyes on what is unseen?

answers.text: Because what is unseen is eternal
Because what is seen is too painful
Because what is seen will fool them

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Instead, Paul says...', 'Nothing tucked away... I know EXACTLY what ends up in the back of a drawer.' and 'ME.' Only the opening card can go past two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The delivery-guy joke shows Paul as the one who serves and delivers, not the one in charge. That points to 'servants' on card 12 and rules out 'leaders' and 'teachers' before the baker reaches the question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Paul says God... in their hearts.', 'Light in the dark?' and 'Friend, after YEARS in a junk drawer... apron.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to finish Paul's line ('hard pressed on all sides, but not ___'). Only the line's own wording decides between crushed, tired and afraid, not any meaning the baker can reason out. This is the same pattern as the Psalm 23 'paths of…' bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This question also asks the baker to finish Paul's line ('struck down, but not what?'). It tests wording, not meaning. The punching-bag joke on card 3 ('popping back up') also points to 'Destroyed' and rules out the other answers.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card puts 'I believed, therefore I have spoken' in quotation marks as what a psalmist says, with the reference Psalm 116:10. BSB Psalm 116:10 reads differently ('I believed, therefore I said...'). The exact quoted wording is only Paul's wording in 2 Corinthians 4:13, where it is introduced as 'what is written.'

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: 'Paul admits their outer self is wasting away' makes it sound like Paul is reluctantly conceding. The text only states it ('Though our outer self is wasting away').

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
